subject: Re: Private Offer — multi-SKU usage floor & channel cost-sharing
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acme.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer details — multi-SKU bundle, usage floor and reseller margin

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with a little more detail on the private offer structure we discussed. Two specific items we need clarity on before legal will sign off: 

1) Usage floor vs. metered overage: We anticipate a heavy initial burst on the embeddings SKU for the first 2 months, then a long tail. We prefer a deal with a modest committed usage floor and simple overage pricing. Can you confirm how a 6-month usage floor would interact with your marketplace billing and whether overage will be invoiced via the marketplace or direct Redwood invoice?

2) Channel cost-sharing: We work with BrightLayer Partners for procurement. The marketplace private offer will route through them — we need confirmation on the reseller uplift and whether Redwood can show a clear breakdown of list price -> BrightLayer fee -> net price to Acme on the offer PDF.

If you can send a draft private offer and a short example invoice that reflects these flows (list price, reseller pass-through, and net), that will help us move to legal.

Appreciate it,
Alex Turner
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme, Inc.

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer details — multi-SKU bundle, usage floor and reseller margin

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short draft and an example invoice that show both flows. Key points up front: 

- We can structure a 6-month committed usage floor for the embeddings SKU and meter the rest at a fixed overage rate. The marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) will handle the invoice routing if the private offer is created through their private-offer mechanism; otherwise, Redwood can invoice directly for dedicated/reseller flows.

- For BrightLayer, we can include an explicit line in the offer PDF for their reseller fee (pass-through) so total list price, reseller fee, and net payable are visible. That pass-through will be implemented as a separate invoice line item in the marketplace offer metadata.

Attachments: ACME_PrivateOffer_Draft_v1.xlsx (draft pricing + SKU bucket), pricing_workback_summary.pdf (summary table and example invoice).

Next steps: Ben from Sales Ops and Irene from Partner Ops are looped in to confirm final margin math and whether BrightLayer needs a separate settlement path. If this looks ok I can convert the draft into a marketplace private offer and share the DocuSign link.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer details — multi-SKU bundle, usage floor and reseller margin

Quick ops note — thanks Lauren. A couple of clarifying questions from my side before we finalize numbers: 

- Is BrightLayer expecting a percentage-based reseller uplift or a flat per-invoice fee? That changes whether we present as a percent pass-through or discrete line.

- For marketplace routing: which cloud marketplace is Acme targeting for procurement (AWS, GCP, or Azure)? Marketplace metered billing vs. direct Redwood invoicing affects the timing of overage charges and revenue recognition.

Also, given the forecasted embedding burst, we recommend a 15% smoothing buffer on the committed floor to avoid frequent overage triggers in months 1–2. If Acme doesn't like buffer, we can present a clean floor + separate explicit one-time spike credit.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, procure@acme.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer details — multi-SKU bundle, usage floor and reseller margin

Ben — thanks. Internal answers copied below and I adjusted the draft.

- BrightLayer confirmed they want a percentage-based uplift (10% of list for channel services). We'll present as a separate "BrightLayer fee" line at 10% so Acme sees list -> channel fee -> net. Irene, please confirm settlement (marketplace settlement vs. partner invoicing).

- Acme intends to use GCP marketplace for this purchase per Alex's original procurement note. That means: the private offer will live in GCP private offers, GCP will bill Acme and remit to Redwood per GCP settlement calendar. Overage will show as marketplace metered usage on monthly GCP invoice. If Acme prefers Redwood invoicing for overage, we can do a hybrid: commit billed via marketplace, overage billed directly. Pros/cons included in the attached summary.

Irene — can you confirm whether BrightLayer needs a separate clearing invoice or if they'll accept GCP remittance and apply their fee off the top? If they require separate billing, we'll need to route as a third-party reseller arrangement (adds ~2–3 week ops lead time).

I've attached pricing_workback_summary.pdf and updated ACME_PrivateOffer_Draft_v1.xlsx (tab named GCP_privateoffer_v1). Changes include: explicit BrightLayer fee at 10%, a 15% smoothing buffer applied to the 6-month embeddings floor and an optional one-time spike credit (pre-authorized) if Acme prefers no buffer.

If all good I can generate the GCP private offer and share the DocuSign/offer link to Acme and BrightLayer.

Thanks — Lauren

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final — GCP private offer draft + next steps (BrightLayer fee included)

Alex / Acme procurement —

Thanks for the speedy responses. Per the internal review we've prepared two options so legal can pick the preferred billing flow:

Option A (Marketplace-native — recommended):
- GCP private offer for 6-month committed embeddings floor (committed units: 1.2M embed-units) with fixed overage rate of $0.0008/embed.
- BrightLayer fee shown as a separate 10% line item in the offer PDF. GCP will bill Acme and remit to Redwood; BrightLayer accepts GCP remittance (no separate clearing invoice required).

Option B (Hybrid — if Acme wants direct overage invoicing):
- Commit billed via GCP private offer; overage billed monthly by Redwood directly. BrightLayer fee handled as separate partner invoice. Adds ~2–3 week ops lead time.

Attached: ACME_PrivateOffer_Draft_v1.xlsx (GCP_privateoffer_v2 tab), pricing_workback_summary.pdf, example_invoice_GCP.pdf.

If Option A is acceptable I'll generate the GCP private offer and send the DocuSign link. If you prefer Option B, let us know and we'll kick off partner ops routing with BrightLayer.

Next action: Alex to confirm preferred option and sign the DocuSign when sent. We have draft DocuSign link ready: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-Private-Offer-2026

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this live.

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
